description: §19.16.2 (S430 round 6) — a `defer` that is the whole UNBRACED body of an `if` (a), an `else` (b) or a loop (l) is E-DEFER-UNSUPPORTED-SITE — three occurrences. For `else` this was load-bearing while the live front-end detached an unbraced `else` arm (g-live-parser-drops-an-unbraced-else-arm-and-runs-it-unconditionally, resolved S437), which would have attached the defer to the function block and run it whether or not `c` holds; the rule stands on its own either way.
rationale: §19.16.2: the unbraced body of an if / else / for / while / do arm is not a stage-1 defer site; it SHALL be a compile error, never silently mis-scoped.
